newsitem.title: USA: New York museum to host Versace exhibition.
newsitem.headline: New York museum to host Versace exhibition.

text.p: The Metroplitan Museum of Art will host an exhibition celebrating the work of slain fashion designer Gianni Versace, officials said on Friday.
The exhibition will open at the museum's Costume Institute on Dec. 11 and remain open through March 22, 1998, they said.
The exhibition also will be the centrepiece of the musuem's annual Costume Institute gala on Dec. 8, traditionally a celebrity-studded social event.

The Versace exhibition will include a small retrospective of the Italian designer's major themes and pieces, and it will trace his inspirations from Greek and Roman classicism and 18th-century court styles to pop artist Andy Warhol and modern abstract art.
Versace was known to visit the landmark museum on Fifth Avenue and was inspired by a recent exhibition that featured Byzantine crosses, Richard Martin, curator of the Costume Institute, said.
The exhibition also will include Versace's recent experiments with new materials such as plastic and metal mesh, he said.
"It is a great privilege to honour this remarkable designer with an exhibition this year," said Martin, who wrote a book published this year entitled "Versace."

The designer was fatally shot on July 15 at his oceanfront mansion in Miami Beach, Florida by alleged spree killer Andrew Cunanan, who committed suicide on Wednesday in a Miami houseboat, authorities said.
The Versace exhibition replaces a previously scheduled exhibition on fashion history that will be rescheduled, the museum said.
